newsitem.title: USA: Amoco sees five-year rise in global output.
newsitem.headline: Amoco sees five-year rise in global output.

text.p: Amoco Corp said Tuesday it forecast worldwide "barrel-oil-equivalent" production to increase from 1996 levels over the next five years with the largest gains expected in the later years.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Amoco said it expects increased output in 1997, with greater amounts coming from the Gulf of Mexico, and first-time production from Colombia, Bolivia and Venezuela.

Amoco's exploration efforts will continue to target those areas offering the most potential and pursue those areas that capitalize on its natural gas resources and continue to expand internationally, the company said in the filing.
In the petroleum products sector, Amoco said it does not anticipate a significant improvement in the U.S. industry refining margins in the near term.

Amoco said its marketing strategy will emphasize brand product quality and growth in its position as a convenience retailer. Strategic alliance with such companies as McDonalds Corp and FEMSA in Mexico are expected to be expanded.

The company and the oil industry will continue to be affected by the volatility of crude oil and natural gas prices, Amoco said. Affecting petroleum products activities is the overall product supply and demand balance.
